name: Mormant

art.title: Mormant, 17 February 1814, at Ten in the Morning

summary: Turning back south after the Six Days, Napoleon's cavalry and Gérard's infantry caught Pahlen's Russian advance guard in the open at Mormant and cut it to pieces.

sources.label: French Order of Battle, Montereau, 17/18 February 1814 (Nafziger Collection 814BDI)

forces.name: Chateau's Division
forces.summary: Victor's first division, which advanced on Mormant at dawn on the right of the road and closed on Pahlen's infantry as the cavalry broke it.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the army on 17 and 18 February, from the French archives; Victor's corps is as of 15 February and the cavalry corps as of 9 February.
Each regiment had one or two battalions here; each is shown as its battalions.
Nafziger names neither brigade's commander.
Nafziger gives the corps no artillery on this return; it is left out.
Two light regiments, where the list allows one in the division, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Dufour's Division
forces.summary: Gérard's first division, which went on with him to Valjouan in the afternoon against Wrede's Bavarians and Austrians.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the army on 17 and 18 February, from the French archives; Victor's corps is as of 15 February and the cavalry corps as of 9 February.

Its battalions were from the depots of a dozen regiments, mostly one from each; each is shown as a regiment of its one battalion. Nafziger names neither the division's commander nor its brigades'; Dufour is from Wikipedia's account.
Nafziger gives Gérard's artillery as four foot companies; one is with each division here, the others in its missing units.
A brigade of four regiments, where the list takes three, and four light battalions, where it allows one light regiment in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Milhaud's Cavalry
forces.summary: Piré's chasseurs and hussars broke Pahlen's cavalry in the open, and Briche's dragoons rode into the Russian squares and closed the road at Grandpuits; L'Héritier's dragoons routed the Cossacks.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the army on 17 and 18 February, from the French archives; Victor's corps is as of 15 February and the cavalry corps as of 9 February.

Piré's light division is Subervie's and Du Coëtlosquet's brigades, Briche's heavy division Montélégier's and Ludot's dragoons, and L'Héritier's Lamotte's and Collaert's. Nafziger names L'Héritier as the corps' commander on 9 February; Wikipedia's account has Milhaud leading it at Mormant, with L'Héritier's division under Kellermann.
The dragoon divisions were veterans brought from Spain that winter.
Its two horse batteries are from Nafziger's return of 25 January, one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.
Four heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, and more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Trelliard's Dragoons
forces.formation: 5th Heavy Cavalry Division, VI Cavalry Corps (Kellermann)
forces.summary: Dragoons brought from Spain, which rode with L'Héritier's division under Kellermann against Pahlen's horse and the Cossacks.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the army on 17 and 18 February, from the French archives; Victor's corps is as of 15 February and the cavalry corps as of 9 February.
Veteran regiments of the army in Spain, sent to Napoleon that winter.
What it did at Mormant is from Wikipedia's account, which doesn't say.

Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, and a cavalry force with no infantry, show as historical departures. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.

toCome.name: Bordesoulle's Detachment
toCome.summary: About five hundred horse, which with Gérard's infantry mauled the Bavarians and Austrians at Valjouan.

toCome.name: The Guard Artillery
toCome.summary: Thirty-six guns pushed up into the front line; the Guard's infantry and cavalry were kept back.

toCome.name: Pahlen's Advance Guard
toCome.formation: Wittgenstein's VI Corps, Army of Bohemia
toCome.summary: Pahlen's hussars and Cossacks with a few battalions of the 3rd, 4th and 14th Divisions, caught in the open at Mormant; the cavalry was broken and the infantry's squares ridden over.

toCome.name: Hardegg's Division
toCome.summary: Fell back through Nangis and was mauled at Valjouan.

toCome.name: Lamotte's Division
toCome.summary: Routed at Valjouan by Gérard's infantry and Bordesoulle's horse.
